summary.headline: PVR INOX Q4 FY26 PAT rose to INR178 crores from a loss of about INR10 crores; FY26 net debt cut to INR161 crores and FCF hit a record INR790 crores.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 25% to INR1,577 crores and EBITDA rose nearly six-fold to INR169 crores, with PAT helped by the gain on divesting 4700BC to Marico. FY26 was the best year on record: 150 million guests (+10%), ATP INR280 (+8%), SPH INR147 (+10%), and IND AS 116-adjusted revenue of INR6,742 crores (+16%). The company pivoted to capital-light formats (55% of 93 FY26 screen additions), cut screen exits to 18 from 72, and reduced net debt to INR161 crores. Management guided FY27 capex to INR375-400 crores and 120+ new screens, with gross debt targeted at about INR500 crores.

segments.name: Exhibition (multiplex operations)
segments.commentary: FY26 footfall 150 million (+10%) and occupancy of 26.2% per management; Q4 footfall 31 million, a record Q4 driven by Dhurandhar: The Revenge, Border 2 and Project Hail Mary.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.commentary: Management called advertising growth subdued this year; Gautam Dutta said Jana Nayagan and Toxic moving out of their slots cost about 7-8% growth, with primary advertising growth expected in H2 from October-December releases.

segments.name: Franchise / FOCO management fees
segments.commentary: FY26 management income close to INR10 crores; run-rate INR13-14 crores per annum, with run-rate growth of 40-50%. Fee is 10-14% of cinema top line.

guidance_outlook: FY27 new screen additions of 100-plus, around 120 visible; 55-60% expected in FOCO and asset-light formats.
FY27 capex INR375-400 crores: about INR225-250 crores new projects, INR80-100 crores renovation, balance maintenance and IT.
Signed capital-light pipeline of 138 screens (52 FOCO, 86 asset-light), expected to execute over about 18 months.
Gross debt about INR760 crores at 31 March 2026, to be brought down to about INR500 crores; net debt to zero possible in 1H FY27 (not committed on timing).
First smart screen pilots to open by mid-July 2026, targeting 28-30 screens this financial year; smart screen capex at least 30-40% below mainstream cinemas.
Capital allocation (dividend or buyback) to be decided by the Board after the company turns net cash; no incremental guidance given.
capex_capacity: FY26: 93 screens added, 55% capital-light (51 screens: 29 asset-light, 22 FOCO); 18 screen exits vs 72 in FY25.
Capex intensity down 24% YoY in FY26.
FY27 capex guided at INR375-400 crores; new screens planned 120+ per year.
Asset-light: developer funds 40-80% of capex; balance capitalised as ROU asset and lease liability, with rent paid as yield.
FOCO: company does not capitalise screens; books only management fee.
demand_pricing: Indian box office FY26 INR13,519 crores, up 11%; Bollywood up 55%, English up 54%.
Mid-scale films grossing INR100-200 crores rose from 12% to 20% share of box office.
Management expects occupancy to rise, citing 470 theatrical vs 30 OTT releases in CY2025 per an EY report (vs 217 vs 105 in CY2022).
Management says IPL has no measurable impact on cinema attendance; IPL playoff matches screened in its cinemas.
Management sees no direct macro impact from West Asia crisis measures; cites cinema as resilient in downturns.
Management says 27-28% occupancy can still deliver pre-COVID EBITDA margins because of post-merger cost efficiencies.

qa_highlights.question: Given debt is negligible, what is FY27 screen addition and own vs asset-light mix, and would dividends follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 120-odd screens in FY27, with 55-60% in FOCO/asset-light; aim to become cash positive, with the Board to decide on accrual use later.

qa_highlights.question: Why pursue asset-light if the balance sheet can fund growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said asset-light and FOCO improve ROCE; own capex will continue in high-competition markets, especially South India, while partner models suit markets with strong share and lower competition.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the FY27 capex INR375-400 crores when most new screens are capital-light?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR225-250 crores for new projects (fit-out payments and handovers), INR80-100 crores for renovations, and the rest for maintenance and IT.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ROU assets fall from about INR4,900 crores to INR4,600 crores despite screen additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation exceeded gross ROU additions; FOCO and asset-light screens add much less ROU than fully leased screens.

qa_highlights.question: Why not a buyback given strong cash flow and low net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the first goal is positive net cash, then the Board will discuss capital allocation; buyback is on the list but no guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How do FOCO economics work for PVR INOX on the P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: Only the management fee (10-14% of top line) is booked; the landlord keeps the property P&L, and PVR INOX incurs no capex or opex on FOCO screens, per management.

risks_watch: Occupancy stuck near 26% (26.2% FY26) despite the target of rising levels; management says 27-28% can restore pre-COVID margins.
Advertising growth subdued; big films shifting dates cut growth by about 7-8%, with dependence on H2 releases.
Macro risk from West Asia crisis and possible fuel price hikes on urban discretionary spend; management says no direct impact seen.
Q4 PAT includes a one-time divestment gain (4700BC to Marico), so underlying earnings are not clear from the call.
Execution of 138 signed capital-light screens over about 18 months and first smart screen pilots by mid-July 2026.
Timing of net-cash status and capital allocation (dividend or buyback) yet to be decided.
Lease and rent cost trend as capital-light share rises; no quantified rent-to-revenue guidance given.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, pipeline and balance sheet, but evasive on capital allocation (buyback/dividend) and on quantifying rent savings and timing of net cash. Management brushed off macro and advertising concerns with qualitative reassurance rather than numbers.
